blocks.text: The valves open and close thousands of times a minute, always at exactly the right moment. A spinning shaft does it: the **camshaft**.

items: As it spins, a bump **pushes its valve open**
When the bump passes, a **spring snaps the valve shut**
A **belt or chain** links it to the crankshaft

blocks.text: Why the cam turns at half speed

items: So the camshaft turns **once** while the crankshaft turns **twice**
The cam gear has **twice as many teeth** as the crank gear

blocks.caption: Top: the crank gear (20 teeth) drives the cam gear (40 teeth). Bottom: one full cam turn, which is one whole cycle.
blocks.narration: Watch the counters. Every time the crankshaft finishes two turns, the camshaft finishes exactly one.

lines: So the cam turns 1 time for every 2 crank turns
blocks.say: Forty teeth divided by twenty teeth is two. So the cam turns once for every two turns of the crank.

blocks.intro: Real valve timing is a bit different from the textbook:
items: Moving air has **momentum**, like water in a hose
Keeping the intake open past the bottom lets air **keep cramming in**
Near the top, **both valves are open at once** for a moment: **valve overlap**
During overlap, the rushing exhaust helps **pull the fresh mix in**

blocks.title: Try it
blocks.text: Flip the lab to **Real** and watch for the yellow overlap wedge at the top.

items: Burning takes a couple of **thousandths of a second**
So the spark fires **before** the top
That makes pressure peak **just after** the top, when it pushes best
Higher RPM = the crank turns further during the burn = spark fires **earlier**

blocks.title: Try it
blocks.text: Drag the **RPM** slider and watch the ⚡ mark move earlier.

lines: A 2 ms burn = 2 × 18° = 36° of crank turn
blocks.say: Three thousand R P M is fifty turns a second, so one turn takes twenty milliseconds. That's eighteen degrees every millisecond. A two millisecond burn means the crank turns thirty six degrees while the fuel is still burning.

blocks.question: The camshaft turns at what speed compared with the crankshaft?
blocks.explain: Half speed: each valve opens once per cycle, and a cycle is two crank turns.

blocks.question: What is valve overlap?
options: Both valves open for a moment near the top, between exhaust and intake
The valves bumping into the piston
The cam turning twice per cycle
blocks.explain: Near the top between exhaust and intake, both are open briefly. The outgoing exhaust helps pull in the fresh mix.

blocks.question: Why does the spark fire before the piston reaches the top?
options: Because burning takes time, so it starts early to peak just after the top
It's a mistake engines just live with
blocks.explain: The burn takes a few milliseconds. Starting early makes the pressure peak right when it can push the piston down.
